extra.message: User-supplied request body is passed directly to node-serialize's unserialize(). node-serialize executes IIFE expressions during unserialization, allowing arbitrary remote code execution via a crafted payload.

The 'url' query parameter is read from the request and passed directly to needle.get() with no validation or allow-list. This endpoint requires no authentication and permits an attacker to make arbitrary server-side HTTP requests (internal port scanning, cloud metadata access, etc.).

Login credentials are passed directly to userSchema.findOne() without sanitization. Because the urlencoded parser uses extended:true, an attacker can send username[$ne]=x&password[$ne]=y to turn the fields into query operators and bypass authentication.

cwe: CWE-943: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements in Data Query Logic

extra.message: The value of req.query.user is passed directly into userSchema.findOne({username: ...}). Query-string parameters can be parsed as MongoDB operator objects (e.g. ?user[$ne]=x), enabling NoSQL injection to retrieve arbitrary user records.

cwe: CWE-943: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements in Data Query Logic

extra.message: The JWT signing secret is hardcoded to the string 'hello'. Anyone who obtains the source can forge valid authentication tokens (including admin tokens), leading to authentication bypass and account takeover.
The 'admin' field is assigned directly from req.body.admin during signup. An attacker can register with admin=true to escalate to administrative privileges (mass assignment / privilege escalation).

The /secret/posts/:username route only verifies that the caller holds a valid JWT, but never checks that the token's username matches the requested :username path parameter. Any authenticated user can view another user's posts (IDOR / broken access control).

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: The full user document (including the password field) is returned verbatim via res.json(result) on an unauthenticated endpoint, disclosing password hashes and other sensitive account data.

extra.message: The 'url' query parameter is reflected directly into an HTML response via response.write() without any HTML encoding, allowing reflected cross-site scripting.

extra.message: A CSRF middleware (csrfProtection) is instantiated but never registered as middleware. State-changing endpoints (login, signup, addpost, forgot password, password reset) rely on cookie-based JWT auth and are vulnerable to cross-site request forgery.

The password-reset link is built using the request Host header (req.get('host')). An attacker can set a malicious Host header so the emailed reset link points to their own server, enabling password-reset token theft and account takeover.

extra.message: The forgot-password endpoint returns a different message depending on whether the email exists in the database, allowing an attacker to enumerate registered accounts.
CORS is enabled with no options (router.use(cors())), which reflects any origin in Access-Control-Allow-Origin, allowing arbitrary sites to read API responses.

cwe: CWE-942: Permissive Cross-domain Policy with Untrusted Domains

extra.message: The 'id' URL parameter is read from location.search and passed directly to eval(). A crafted link (e.g. /home?id=alert(document.cookie)) executes arbitrary JavaScript in the victim's browser (reflected DOM XSS / code injection).
